messages:
acme_ops: Hey team — our Private deployment in us-east-1 started failing to pull model shards around 08:12 UTC. Clients see intermittent TLS handshake failures and a bunch of resets. curl -v to https://control.redwood.ai/health returns "Connection reset by peer". Any idea?
oliver_support: Sorry you're hitting this — we'll take a look. Can you paste the curl -v output + any NAT/NACL/SG changes in the last hour? Also which subnets/VPC are you using? :eyes:
acme_ops: curl -v output attached (trimmed):
```
* Connected to control.redwood.ai (52.20.11.123) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake: alert unknown ca
* SSL certificate problem: self signed certificate in certificate chain
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: self signed certificate in certificate chain
```
We haven't changed infra. Using private subnets behind a NAT gateway (10.0.0.0/16 VPC). SG egress is open to 0.0.0.0/0:443. NACL is default except a custom outbound rule that restricts ephemeral ports — but that was added weeks ago and seemed fine until now.
jordan_sre: Two quick checks: 1) Are you resolving control.redwood.ai to an internal IP (corporate DNS rewrite)? 2) Is there a transparent TLS proxy/SSL inspection in your path that could present a different cert? The curl output looks like MITM/inspection. Also, NACL restricting ephemeral ports can break TCP 3-way for NATted connections.
chris_neteng: Can you run: `dig +short control.redwood.ai` and `traceroute -n control.redwood.ai` from a failing host? Also `sudo conntrack -L | grep 52.20.11.123` to see if conntrack entries are stuck.
acme_ops: dig returns 52.20.11.123 (public). traceroute shows first hop to our NAT gateway then stops. We don't have an inline SSL proxy as far as our stack team knows, but the cert chain in curl shows a corp CA.
oliver_support: That points at your egress path doing TLS inspection. If inspection rewrites the cert, control plane will reject the connection from Redwood side (SNI mismatch or ALPN mismatch). However the "Connection reset by peer" and intermittent resets could also be from our side if we see client IPs changing because of SNAT churn.
jordan_sre: Quick repro steps we suggest: 1) From a host, `curl -v --resolve control.redwood.ai:443:52.20.11.123 https://control.redwood.ai/health` to bypass DNS-based rewrites. 2) If that succeeds, the issue is DNS/HTTP proxy. 3) If it fails, capture tcpdump: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 52.20.11.123 and port 443 -w /tmp/rdw.pcap` and share the pcap with us.
acme_ops: We tried `--resolve` and the TLS handshake completes, health returns 200. So DNS/proxy is the culprit. Our infra team says we recently pushed a transparent proxy update that enforces company CA for outbound TLS.
chris_neteng: Ok that's consistent. Transparent SSL inspection will break our mTLS/expected cert chain for some endpoints. Two remediation paths: 1) Add control.redwood.ai to your proxy bypass/allowlist so passthrough TLS goes direct; 2) If you must inspect, configure the proxy to trust Redwood's CA or perform TLS passthrough for our endpoints.
oliver_support: Also confirm your NACL ephemeral port rule allows high ports for return traffic (1024-65535 or standard ephemeral range). We saw similar symptoms when return ports were blocked and the NAT gateway retried sessions causing resets.
acme_ops: Fingers crossed — we're opening a bypass for control.redwood.ai via the proxy team now. We'll also relax the outbound NACL ephemeral range to 32768-61000 temporarily and report back.
deploy-bot: @channel Notice: control-plane health check for customer-acme succeeded at 09:35 UTC after route change.
acme_ops: Confirmed — model pulls resumed and no more TLS errors. Huge thanks everyone. :tada:
oliver_support: Glad that fixed it. Leaving this open for 24h to monitor; if you want we can run a packet capture during the next window to confirm no intermittent drops.
jordan_sre: Notes for the runbook: add a checkbox for "verify no TLS interception on egress" and "ensure ephemeral port ranges allowed in NACL for NATted subnets". I'll update the KB. :memo:
